documents.body: Biomarker results are back for case M-2417: EGFR exon 19 deletion, PD-L1 40%. The chart recommends the standard chemo-immunotherapy regimen starting next week. M-2417 is a 61-year-old with IIIB lung adenocarcinoma, good performance status, no brain metastases on last MRI. The tumor board question is whether to start the standard regimen or wait for the molecular tumor board, which meets in nine days and tends to favor targeted combinations for EGFR-mutant cases. Fictional clinical data.
documents.title: M-2417 chart note

documents.body: Imaging addendum for M-2417, October 26. Primary right upper lobe mass 4.1 cm, ipsilateral mediastinal nodes positive, no distant disease. Response assessment will follow RECIST 1.1 with the first restaging scan at nine weeks. The radiologist flags that programs with biomarker-driven combinations usually repeat imaging earlier, at six weeks, because response shows sooner. Fictional clinical data.
documents.title: M-2417 imaging addendum

documents.body: Case M-2420: 58-year-old with resected IIA colon adenocarcinoma, considering adjuvant chemotherapy. Pathology shows no high-risk features; the estimated benefit of adjuvant treatment is small. The question for review is whether ctDNA monitoring can safely replace adjuvant therapy here. Fictional clinical data.
documents.title: M-2420 workup note

documents.body: Attending-only consult notes, October. The EGFR trial slot situation is tight: one osimertinib-combination slot left this quarter, two attendings holding candidates. If M-2417 starts standard chemo-immunotherapy next week, the trial option closes, because the trial requires treatment-naive patients. Nobody outside attendings has seen the slot count. Helen's read: the board should sequence the decision, trial eligibility first, regimen second, and whoever announces the sequence owns the delay.
documents.title: Consult notes: EGFR trial slot (attendings only)
